links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answers across repeated queries in separate sessions
links.effect: Reproducibility ≈90% ChatGPT, ≈85% Gemini, ≈83% DeepSeek; not perfectly consistent across repeated runs.
links.quote: ChatGPT achieved the highest overall accuracy (≈92%) and reproducibility (≈90%), followed by Gemini (≈88% accuracy; ≈85% reproducibility) and DeepSeek (≈86% accuracy; ≈83% reproducibility).

links.outcome: Omission of clinically relevant information and lower accuracy on diagnosis questions
links.effect: Omission of clinically relevant information was the most common limitation; accuracy was lower across models for diagnosis and clinical assessment questions. DeepSeek had more factual inaccuracies.
links.quote: Qualitative error analysis indicated that the omission of clinically relevant information was the most common limitation, while DeepSeek produced more factual inaccuracies and Gemini more generalized guidance.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of three LLMs answering parent-centered questions about anorexia nervosa, evaluated by expert psychiatrists for quality, usefulness, and reliability without testing a specific organizational deployment practice.
